Layout and light: U1 to U10

2026-10-22 · What changed is boxed in red. Taken from the running app on stand-ins, so nothing was paid for. The “before” shots were taken first, on episode #3. Every moving effect is drawn on this computer and left out when Windows is set to show no animation.

The header: one Make button, and the title has its room back (U1)

Record voices, Generate pictures and Make it all were three buttons for one job. Now one button does the next thing still to make (here, Record voices; on a finished episode, Make a draft), and its menu has each job and All of it. Before, in a narrower window the episode title shrank to “T..”.

One dialog for the series and the look (U2)

The ⋯ menu had eleven items, three of them separate dialogs for the channel, the host and the look and mix. Now it has five, and Series and look holds all three as tabs.

A floating bar for jobs and messages, and a strip along the foot (U3)

The job panel and the message bar used to appear above the page and push it down. They now float over its foot, so nothing moves. An outcome goes by itself after ten seconds; an error stays. Offline and the messages to read back sit at the bottom left, beside the build version.

Teaser cards shaped like phones (U4) and captions set on the preview (U5)

The old card's picture was 260 by 120, wider than tall, though it stood for an upright video (no before shot: the old cards are gone). Now each card is a 9:16 poster with its hook across the top as the teaser shows it, and each moment is a strip you drag along its clip. The caption controls moved onto the preview (Aa), and Render master video stays at the column's foot.

The deck: a fluid you can stir, a thread through the cards, and the clips end to end (U6, U7, U9)

The cloud of light behind the deck is now a real fluid, worked out on the graphics card: it carries itself along, its whirls are kept alive, and it cannot be squeezed. The pointer stirs it, a dragged card pulls a wake, and a finished clip sends out swirls. A thread runs behind the glass from card to card in running order. Below, the clips lie end to end against the series' three to five minutes. Fixed on the way: in a wider window the cards stayed where they were (before, three columns and a gap), because their glide never reached its end.

The R1 as a hologram (U8)

In the room below the saved episodes, the R1 turns on a projector, drawn by casting rays into a scene of soft solid shapes, with scan lines, a rim of light and the odd slip of a projected picture. It rehearses what the lesson box says, and changes as you type.

The finished video's thumbnail gathers itself (U10)

When the master is finished, some twenty thousand motes, one for each point of the thumbnail, swirl in from all round the window and settle into the picture. A sweep of light crosses it, and then the confetti and fanfare as before. Taken from a stand-in render of the one-clip episode, which was copied aside first and put back exactly.
